task.name: The dev agent cannot execute the project's declared toolchain, so it iterates blind against the gate
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A dev agent working on a project whose verification requires the host Apple
toolchain cannot execute that toolchain, and so cannot run the builds or tests
that will judge its work. It edits, submits, and learns the outcome only from the
coordinator's gate.

In adopter run `0ea58a758f52` (story `issue-230`) this produced six dev
iterations and $46.40 of dev spend against six consecutive gate failures on Swift
compile errors, every iteration derived from gate traces rather than from running
the code.

Run `5096bd4a46e3` (story `issue-248`) records why, in the dev's own handoff:

> this agent runs inside an outer macOS sandbox, and SwiftPM compiles package
> manifests via `sandbox-exec`, so nested sandboxing fails with
> `sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`

The same handoff confirms the failure persists with the agent sandbox both
enabled and disabled, with `-disableAutomaticPackageResolution
-onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile -skipPackageUpdates`, and against
already-resolved derived data with all five package checkouts present. Apple's
own documented workaround for the nesting collision,
`defaults write com.apple.dt.Xcode IDEPackageSupportDisableManifestSandbox`, is
itself denied with `Could not write domain com.apple.dt.Xcode`.

## Expected behavior

A dev agent must be able to execute the commands a project declares as its
verification. An agent that cannot run what will judge it can only guess, and
every iteration it spends is an unverified proposal rather than a tested change —
which is the failure mode the iteration budget exists to bound, not to fund. Where
a host isolation mechanism is structurally incompatible with a project's declared
toolchain, that incompatibility should be resolvable by the project rather than
absorbed as permanent blindness in the dev loop, and it should never be left to
surface as iteration exhaustion.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** dev iterates against a toolchain it cannot invoke,
  accruing cost per iteration with no execution feedback, until the iteration
  pool is exhausted.

- **Evidence:** forge confines agents with `sandbox-exec` on macOS
  (`src/theforge/config/auth.py:34`, `src/theforge/runners/runner_gemini.py:132`,
  `src/theforge/coordinator/dev_phase.py:736`). SwiftPM invokes `sandbox-exec` to
  compile package manifests, and macOS refuses to apply a sandbox inside a
  sandbox. The `xcode` preset already grants the four relevant write roots
  (`~/Library/Developer`, `~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm`,
  `~/Library/org.swift.swiftpm`, `~/Library/Caches/com.apple.dt.Xcode`) and the
  `com.apple.CoreSimulator.CoreSimulatorService` mach service, so the denial is
  not an allowlist gap. `~/Library/Preferences` is not granted, which is why the
  documented Xcode workaround is denied as well.

- **Ruled out:** not network egress — package resolution failed against fully
  cached, already-resolved checkouts. Not a missing write root or mach service —
  the relevant grants are present and the failure occurs in sandbox application
  itself. Not a toolchain flag or configuration problem — the dev exercised the
  documented flags and the documented escape hatch, and recorded both outcomes.

- **Confirmed cause:** the collision is in the isolation mechanism rather than in
  its allowlist. A toolchain that itself invokes `sandbox-exec` cannot run inside
  a `sandbox-exec` confinement, and no grant expressible in the preset model
  changes that.

- **Affected code path:** the dev-phase sandbox wrapper
  (`coordinator/dev_phase.py`), sandbox availability resolution
  (`config/auth.py`), and the preset model (`config/sandbox_capabilities`).

- **Fix-success criterion:** for a project declaring an Apple toolchain, a dev
  iteration completes a real app-target build and test within the run, while
  activity outside the project's declared toolchain commands remains confined.

## Notes

**Settled by [ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-dev-phase-verification-capability.md) (Accepted 2026-07-29).** The decision: the project
defines unconfined commands TheForge can run, and the coordinator gives the agent
access to request that these be run on its behalf. The agent's granted capability is
the request, never the execution — seatbelt confinement is a property of the process
tree (`runners/sandbox.py:549`), so no allowlist can un-confine a child. The declared
unit is a whole named command, not a binary, so argv stays out of agent control.
Implement against that decision; the design is no longer open here.

Retained for context — the considerations the ADR weighed: the coordinator already executes
project-authored shell outside the agent sandbox when it runs `gate_command`, so
elevating declared toolchain commands would not introduce a new class of exposure,
though it would change how often that exposure occurs. Any such elevation has to
account for the fact that build systems execute repository files the dev agent can
edit — `Package.swift`, `project.pbxproj` run-script phases, and the `Makefile`
itself — so trust in a toolchain binary does not transfer to an invocation whose
inputs the agent authored. Network egress is separable from this and was not
required in the observed runs.

Relates to #2038, which records the same ceiling from the capability-model side.

handoff.summary: Implemented ADR-0007's coordinator-mediated dev verification capability. Projects declare whole named commands under validation.dev_verification_commands in forge.yaml; a new coordinator-owned broker (coordinator/dev_verification.py) watches a per-iteration request directory in the worktree while the dev agent runs, accepts only declared names, executes the configured command through the same unsandboxed shell primitive the gate uses, and writes an atomic response artifact carrying exit code, timeout flag, output tail, and a trace path. The broker is constructed before prompt routing, started before the run_agent retry loop, and stopped in a finally, so its lifetime spans the whole iteration and the fail-closed per-iteration request budget (which counts refusals too) does not reset across transport retries. Dev and fix prompts gained a shared verification section listing declared names and the write-request/poll-response protocol, via keyword-only params defaulting off so cli/shared.py needed no change. Every request is recorded per dev iteration and at run level in the audit record, which required an audit schema bump to v15 with a reader-side migration helper. Load-time validation rejects empty/traversing names, empty commands, unknown fields, and non-positive limits. Declaring nothing keeps existing behavior exactly: no channel directory, no prompt section, no change to dev sandbox resolution.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: For a project declaring an Apple toolchain, a dev iteration completes a real app-target build and test within the run, while activity outside the project's declared toolchain commands remains confined.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The mechanism is complete and seam-tested: a dev agent that cannot execute the toolchain requests a declared command by name, the coordinator runs it outside the sandbox, and the result flows back into the same iteration (tests/test_coord_dev_verification_seam.py). The confinement half is proven directly — a seam test asserts state.sandboxed, dev_containment, and dev_sandbox_capabilities are byte-identical to a run without the capability, so nothing outside the declared commands was un-confined. Marked PARTIAL rather than MET only because the end-to-end claim names a real Apple toolchain: that is provable only in an adopter run on macOS with Xcode installed, which this repository's gate cannot exercise. No code path is missing for it.

deferred_items: Option B from ADR-0007 (transparent PATH-shim interception) is explicitly a later ergonomic layer over this mediated path, not part of this increment.

17 pre-existing test failures in test_cut_rc_isolation.py / test_sprint_lock.py / test_sprint_reexec_collision.py fail under this agent's sandbox with 'Operation not permitted' (multiprocessing semaphores, mktemp in /var/folders). Untouched by this change; expected to pass in the coordinator's unsandboxed gate run.

handoff.summary: Fixed both P1 review findings from cycle 1. (1) TIMEOUT_RESUME is the only DEV route without a prompt builder, so a resumed agent was never told about the fresh per-iteration verification channel the coordinator had opened; the rendered verification section is now appended to the resume prompt from a single shared _verification_channel dict that the prompt builders also consume, so the two routes cannot describe different channels. (2) DevVerificationBroker.stop() joined for a fixed 30s and returned without ever terminating the in-flight subprocess, letting an unconfined build outlive the iteration and race the coordinator's authoritative gate while its record vanished from the audit trail; shutdown is now bounded and terminal — a grace period, then a process-group kill via the coordinator's existing _kill_process_group helper, with the real outcome recorded as cancelled: true (distinct from timed_out and from an ordinary non-zero exit, since a kill is not a verdict on the code), plus a synthetic backfilled record if the serving thread never lands one. Cancellation required a handle on the live process, so util._run_shell_detailed gained a keyword-only on_process_start observation hook defaulting to None with no behavior change for existing callers. Also fixed an adjacent defect the work exposed: the shutdown drain poll used to execute a request that arrived as the iteration ended, starting a long unconfined build with nobody left to read it; it now refuses with iteration_ended and still audits the request. Six new tests cover exactly the gaps the reviewers named.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: For a project declaring an Apple toolchain, a dev iteration completes a real app-target build and test within the run, while activity outside the project's declared toolchain commands remains confined.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The mechanism is complete and seam-tested, and now covers every DEV route: normal, fix/P2-cleanup, and timeout-resume iterations all carry the request channel. The confinement half is proven directly — a seam test asserts state.sandboxed, dev_containment, and dev_sandbox_capabilities are identical to a run without the capability, so nothing outside the declared commands was un-confined. This iteration additionally guarantees no declared command outlives the iteration that requested it, which matters for the AC's second clause: an unconfined build still running during the coordinator's gate would make the gate measure a tree the build was mutating. Still PARTIAL only because the end-to-end claim names a real Apple toolchain, provable only in an adopter run on macOS with Xcode — this repository's gate cannot exercise it. No code path is missing.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5] The mediated verification path is implemented for the normal DEV prompt, but it misses timeout-resume DEV iterations and can lose in-flight unconfined command results. | [google-gemini-3.5-flash] The coordinator-mediated dev verification capability is beautifully implemented, fully compliant with ADR-0007, and thoroughly tested. | [claude-sonnet] Coordinator-mediated verification broker is well-designed and audited for the fast path, but stop() never kills an in-flight declared command, so a build can outlive the dev iteration and race the authoritative gate while its outcome silently drops from the audit trail.

findings.description: When a timed-out DEV attempt resumes on a project with declared verification commands, the coordinator creates a fresh per-iteration broker but sends only the timeout continuation text, so the agent is not told the current request and response paths or the declared command names.

If the agent exits while a requested verification command is still running, broker shutdown waits only thirty seconds, then the DEV phase snapshots the records before the command has produced a response or audit entry.

DevVerificationBroker.stop() sets a stop event and joins its serving thread for a fixed 30 seconds, then returns unconditionally, without ever terminating the subprocess a declared command may still be running.

ac_verification.evidence: src/theforge/coordinator/dev_phase.py:833-858 constructs the broker and passes channel metadata into normal dev and fix prompt builders at lines 883-904, 911-931, 946-972, and 993-1019; src/theforge/coordinator/dev_verification.py:282-324 executes declared command names through _run_shell_detailed and writes response artifacts; tests/test_coord_dev_verification_seam.py:133-252 covers the normal prompt, accepted/refused requests, unchanged sandbox state, and audit recording. Missing: src/theforge/coordinator/dev_phase.py:874-881 omits the verification section for TIMEOUT_RESUME prompts, and src/theforge/coordinator/dev_verification.py:165-175 can return from stop before an in-flight command has produced the result that should flow back into the same iteration.; The broker is implemented in src/theforge/coordinator/dev_verification.py and integrated into the dev phase in src/theforge/coordinator/dev_phase.py. Seam-level integration tests in tests/test_coord_dev_verification_seam.py verify that a dev agent can request a declared command by name, the coordinator executes it outside the sandbox, and the result flows back into the iteration, while the agent's process tree remains sandboxed. Unit tests in tests/test_dev_verification_broker.py cover the broker's request/response protocol, fail-closed budget, and config validation.; tests/test_coord_dev_verification_seam.py and tests/test_dev_verification_broker.py demonstrate the request/response protocol, refusal of undeclared names, the fail-closed budget, and that state.sandboxed/dev_containment/dev_sandbox_capabilities are unchanged by the capability — covering the confinement half convincingly. The build/test-completion half cannot be proven in this repository without a real Apple toolchain, which the dev's own handoff acknowledges. Additionally, no test covers the stop()-timeout race described above, so the "auditable by construction" property this criterion depends on is not fully verified even within what this repo's tests can reach.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [claude-opus] Step 2/Step 4 define the request/response artifact protocol but not how the agent blocks between writing a request and reading the response. The broker only observes the request directory while run_agent is in flight, so a dev agent that writes a request and immediately continues will read a missing or stale response.
  Suggestion: Have the broker write the response atomically (temp file + rename) under a request-derived name, and have the prompt instruct the agent to poll for that exact path with a bounded sleep loop; treat a missing response after the configured timeout as a failed request rather than silence.
- [P1-impl] [claude-opus] Step 3 places broker start/stop around run_agent, but dev_phase.py:1035-1060 calls run_agent inside a transport-retry while True: loop. A broker started once per iteration must tolerate multiple run_agent attempts, and per-iteration request limits need a defined reset point across retries.
  Suggestion: Scope broker lifetime to the whole iteration (outside the retry loop) with the finally-stop, and state explicitly whether the request budget resets on a transport retry.
- [P2] [claude-opus] Step 4 modifies build_dev_prompt/build_fix_prompt, but the plan lists only dev_phase.py call sites (dev_phase.py:844, 871, 905, 951). There is a fourth caller at src/theforge/cli/shared.py:368 that is not mentioned.
  Suggestion: Keep the new prompt parameters keyword-only with an off-by-default value (as the existing signature style already does) so cli/shared.py:368 needs no change; note this explicitly so the dev agent does not make the parameter required.
- [P2] [claude-opus] Step 1 names src/theforge/config/schema.py's test (tests/test_config_schema.py) but not where strict validation actually lives. config/schema.py holds v0.8 model-list config dataclasses, not forge.yaml key validation; the validation-section parsing and stale/unknown-key rejection are in config/load.py around lines 669-680 alongside the existing _validate_gate_timeout-style helpers.
  Suggestion: Add the new load-time validators next to the existing validation.* helpers in load.py (load.py:520-600) and extend the stale-key guard at load.py:669-678 rather than touching config/schema.py.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Implement ADR-0007 as a coordinator-side verification broker: projects declare whole named verification commands in forge.yaml, and dev agents request those names through a file-backed request channel while their normal process tree remains sandboxed. Keep execution, policy limits, output capture, and audit ownership in coordinator code rather than runner policy.

steps.description: Add typed configuration for project-declared dev verification commands.
steps.details: Extend ValidationConfig with a strict mapping of named dev verification commands. Each entry should be a whole shell command plus bounded timeout/output settings; reject unknown fields, empty names, empty commands, non-positive limits, and malformed structures at load time. Do not alter gate_command semantics or sandbox capability presets.

steps.description: Create the coordinator-owned verification request executor.
steps.details: Add a small broker that watches a per-iteration request directory under the worktree, accepts only declared command names, runs the configured command through the existing coordinator shell helper outside the dev sandbox, writes a response artifact with exit code, timeout status, output tail, and trace path, and enforces per-iteration request limits fail-closed. The agent controls only the declared name, never argv or shell text.

steps.description: Wire the broker into DEV iteration lifecycle.
steps.details: Start the verification broker immediately before run_agent and stop it in a finally block after the agent returns. Pass the request directory and declared command names into prompt construction only when commands are configured. Preserve the existing dev sandbox resolution and runner invocation so ordinary agent activity remains confined.

steps.description: Teach dev and fix prompts how to request declared verification.
steps.details: Add a concise section listing available verification command names and the request/response file protocol. Instruct agents to request these commands by name for sandbox-incompatible toolchain feedback, to read the response artifact, and not to invent argv or run the full gate directly. Keep existing gate delegation language intact.

steps.description: Expose verification requests in audit output.
steps.details: Record each request with iteration, command name, accepted/refused status, exit code, timeout flag, output truncation, and trace path. Avoid logging secret values beyond what command output already emits through existing gate-style tail handling.

steps.description: Add a seam-level integration test proving the dev loop can consume coordinator-run verification.
steps.details: Use the existing fake runner style to simulate a dev agent writing a verification request file and reading the response before handoff. Assert the declared command ran outside the agent path, unknown command names are refused, request limits are enforced, the normal dev sandbox state is unchanged, and audit telemetry contains the real request/result.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A dev agent must be able to execute the commands a project declares as its verification.

For a project declaring an Apple toolchain, a dev iteration completes a real app-target build and test within the run, while activity outside the project's declared toolchain commands remains confined.

risks.description: The exact request-channel shape was left out of scope by the ADR.
risks.mitigation: Use a minimal file-backed protocol because it works for CLI and API agents without provider-specific tool plumbing, and keep the protocol documented only in the dev prompt and broker tests.

risks.description: Coordinator-run commands execute repository-authored files that the dev agent can edit.
risks.mitigation: Match the accepted gate exposure: only project-declared whole commands run, argv stays out of agent control, request count is bounded, and every invocation is audited.

risks.description: Long-running Apple builds can outlive or hang the dev iteration.
risks.mitigation: Use command-level timeouts and existing process-group cleanup through the coordinator shell helper; always stop the broker in dev_phase finally handling.
